title: Boolean existential over a list is false when the predicate always fails
statement: Let $l$ be a finite list of elements of a type $\alpha$, and let $p \colon \alpha \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ be a Boolean predicate. If $p(x) = \mathrm{false}$ for every entry $x$ of $l$, then the Boolean existential $\bigvee_{x \in l} p(x)$ — the value $\mathrm{true}$ exactly when some entry of $l$ satisfies $p$ — is $\mathrm{false}$.
hypotheses_covered: p(x) = false for every element x of the list l
replaced:
If a Boolean predicate $p$ is false on every element of a list $l$, then $l.\mathrm{any}\,p$
is false.
